<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="טבת_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916134_theRebbe_917" batchId="meluket-_D7_98_D7_91_D7_AA_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916134_theRebbe_917__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the unique nature of Torah, which is G‑d’s wisdom transcending human intellect, so that the Torah learned in youth remains unchanged even in old age, and this is illustrated through the ascent of Metat from Yetzirah to Atzilus.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter in more detail</t>
    <t s="2">will be understood based on what the Tzemach Tzedek wrote in the maamar</t>
    <t s="3">beginning with the words “To understand the matter of our Sages’ statement”</t>
    <t s="4">that the light of Ein Sof, blessed be He, is above without end and below without limit.</t>
    <t s="5">[This heichel</t>
    <t s="6">(in which the aforementioned maamar is found)</t>
    <t s="7">was in captivity for several years,</t>
    <t s="8">and recently</t>
    <t s="9">it was redeemed from captivity and arrived here.</t>
    <t s="10">And it is noteworthy</t>
    <t s="11">that in this discourse there are several matters that are not in the aforementioned discourses.]</t>
    <t s="12">In explanation of the verse</t>
    <t s="13">“Train a youth according to his way; even when he grows old he will not depart from it,”</t>
    <t s="14">for at first glance, when a person grows old he should ascend to a higher level,</t>
    <t s="15">and what is</t>
    <t s="16">the advantage that even when he grows old he will not depart from the way he was trained as a youth?</t>
    <t s="17">And he explains in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="18">that in human intellect there is a great and immense difference between the intellect a person attains in his youth and the intellect he attains in his adulthood, and all the more so in his old age.</t>
    <t s="19">But in the Torah, which is G‑dliness,</t>
    <t s="20">the difference between his youth and his old age is only in the comprehension of the person in which the Torah is clothed,</t>
    <t s="21">but in the Torah itself,</t>
    <t s="22">which is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He, above the intellect of created beings,</t>
    <t s="23">there is no difference between the intellect of the youth and the intellect of the elder,</t>
    <t s="24">and therefore even when he grows old he will not depart from the way he was taught in his youth.</t>
    <t s="25">And he adds in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="26">that it is written</t>
    <t s="27">“I was a youth and also have aged,”</t>
    <t s="28">“youth” refers to Metat in Yetzirah, and “I have aged” refers to his ascent in Atzilus,</t>
    <t s="29">for the wisdom of Torah that is in Atzilus is far higher than the wisdom of Torah that is in Yetzirah.</t>
    <t s="30">And nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="31">even when he grows old and ascends to Atzilus, he will not depart from the way he was taught in his youth in Yetzirah,</t>
    <t s="32">because the essence of Torah is the essential delight of the Awtsmoos</t>
    <t s="33">(and “I was with Him, [a source of] delight,”</t>
    <t s="34">specifically “with Him”),</t>
    <t s="35">which is above even the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="36">the Chochmah of Atzilus.</t>
    <t s="37">And regarding this aspect of Torah</t>
    <t s="38">(which is the essence of Torah)</t>
    <t s="39">there is no difference between the comprehension of Yetzirah</t>
    <t s="40">(and also the comprehension of human intellect)</t>
    <t s="41">and the comprehension of Atzilus.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the advantage of Torah over prayer is that Torah draws down G‑dliness itself, which remains G‑d’s wisdom even below, transcending the distinctions of worlds.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, the advantage in the drawing down through Torah over the drawing down through prayer will be understood even more.</t>
    <t s="1">For the drawing down below through prayer is</t>
    <t s="2">(not that G‑dliness itself is drawn down below,</t>
    <t s="3">but rather)</t>
    <t s="4">that through the drawing down a change is made in the matters of the world.</t>
    <t s="5">And the drawing down of Torah</t>
    <t s="6">is a drawing down of G‑dliness,</t>
    <t s="7">such that even after its descent below it is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="8">And moreover,</t>
    <t s="9">the G‑dliness that is in Torah, which is drawn down below and clothed in the intellect of the person studying it,</t>
    <t s="10">is not in the category of worlds,</t>
    <t s="11">therefore,</t>
    <t s="12">the comprehension of human intellect and the comprehension of Atzilus are truly equal with respect to it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the advantage of prayer over Torah is that prayer effects a revealed change in the lower creations, and that even in an individual’s prayer the influence is drawn down, though it may be in concealment.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that just as the advantage in the drawing down through Torah over the drawing down through prayer is with regard to the recipient below,</t>
    <t s="3">in that a revelation of G‑dliness is drawn into him,</t>
    <t s="4">so too is the advantage in the drawing down through prayer over the drawing down through Torah,</t>
    <t s="5">for in addition to the fact that the source of the drawing down through prayer is above the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="6">the advantage in the drawing down through prayer is also with regard to the recipient below,</t>
    <t s="7">in that through prayer a change is made in the created beings below,</t>
    <t s="8">to heal the sick and bless the years.</t>
    <t s="9">And to add,</t>
    <t s="10">that this matter</t>
    <t s="11">[that through prayer a change is made below]</t>
    <t s="12">applies to every prayer.</t>
    <t s="13">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="14">that it is explained in the aforementioned discourse of the Tzemach Tzedek,</t>
    <t s="15">that regarding what is stated in the Gemara</t>
    <t s="16">that in communal prayer</t>
    <t s="17">(specifically)</t>
    <t s="18">it is written</t>
    <t s="19">“Behold, G‑d is mighty, He does not</t>
    <t s="20">despise,”</t>
    <t s="21">that it is desirable and accepted forever,</t>
    <t s="22">the intention in this is,</t>
    <t s="23">that this—that the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills the request of communal prayer—</t>
    <t s="24">is also in a revealed manner.</t>
    <t s="25">That is to say,</t>
    <t s="26">that even in an individual’s prayer,</t>
    <t s="27">the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills his request</t>
    <t s="28">[as is proven from the fact that the Men of the Great Assembly instituted praying three times every day,</t>
    <t s="29">and certainly they would not have instituted a blessing that would be, G‑d forbid, in vain].</t>
    <t s="30">Rather, in an individual’s prayer,</t>
    <t s="31">it is possible that the influence</t>
    <t s="32">(the fulfillment of the request)</t>
    <t s="33">will be in concealment,</t>
    <t s="34">and the advantage of communal prayer is that the influence is in revelation.</t>
    <t s="35">And it is noteworthy,</t>
    <t s="36">that in several discourses</t>
    <t s="37">it is explained that in an individual’s prayer it is possible that the influence remains above and is not drawn down below,</t>
    <t s="38">but in the aforementioned discourse of the Tzemach Tzedek it is explained that the influence</t>
    <t s="39">(even in an individual’s prayer)</t>
    <t s="40">is drawn down below,</t>
    <t s="41">except that it is possible that it is in concealment.</t>
    <t s="42">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="43">that since the request of prayer is that the influence be drawn down below</t>
    <t s="44">(to heal the sick and bless the years),</t>
    <t s="45">therefore,</t>
    <t s="46">even if they draw down for him the influence he requested, but the influence is not drawn down below,</t>
    <t s="47">his prayer would be a blessing in vain,</t>
    <t s="48">and from this it is proven,</t>
    <t s="49">that in every prayer,</t>
    <t s="50">even in an individual’s prayer, the influence is drawn down below, except that it is possible that it is in concealment.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
